ACCT 1010.title: Accounting, Business and Society
ACCT 1010.description: Overview of accounting in business and social contexts; use of accounting information for accountability and decision-making in companies, non-profit organizations, and government; major elements of accounting, including assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses; discharge of accountability by companies through corporate social and environmental reports. The aim of this course is to make students aware of how accounting could be applicable to fundamental business transactions and ways to evaluate how businesses are operated.
cilos: List the broad framework of ethics, corporate governance, and corporate social responsibility, while demonstrating the knowledge and respect of ethics and ethical standards in accounting in particular
Explain the roles of accounting in business and social contexts; and their bearings on corporate social and environmental accounting
Identify the different users of accounting information and their information needs; and the approaches to use the information in financial statements according to their needs
Identify and describe broad aspects of appropriate accounting treatments for different transactions of different organisations, and how such may address stakeholders’ information needs
Read, interpret, and analyze financial statements, including the balance sheet, the income statement, and the cash flow statements

ACCT 1010.title: Accounting, Business and Society
ACCT 1010.description: Overview of accounting in business and social contexts; use of accounting information for accountability and decision-making in companies, non-profit organizations, and government; major elements of accounting, including assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses; discharge of accountability by companies through corporate social and environmental reports. The aim of this course is to make students aware of how accounting could be applicable to fundamental business transactions and ways to evaluate how businesses are operated.
cilos: List the broad framework of ethics, corporate governance, and corporate social responsibility, while demonstrating the knowledge and respect of ethics and ethical standards in accounting in particular
Explain the roles of accounting in business and social contexts; and their bearings on corporate social and environmental accounting
Identify the different users of accounting information and their information needs; and the approaches to use the information in financial statements according to their needs
Identify and describe broad aspects of appropriate accounting treatments for different transactions of different organisations, and how such may address stakeholders’ information needs
Read, interpret, and analyze financial statements, including the balance sheet, the income statement, and the cash flow statements

ACCT 1610.title: Laws in Society and Business
ACCT 1610.description: This course provides an introduction to law and business society. Topics include general introduction to the concepts in law; an introduction to the Hong Kong legal system under the principle of "one country, two systems"; copyright law; trademark law; agency law; insolvency law; employment law and business ethics. As Hong Kong is a well-developed business society, this course is intended to build students' understanding of the relationship between the law and the society and discuss laws in society and business.
cilos: To build students’ understanding of the relationship between the law and the society
To enhance selected skills like analytical and critical thinking, effective communication and team work
To discuss the importance of ethical responsibility and apply the ethical standard to resolve the dilemmas
To analyze the law of agency and attain a balance between the principal and the agent
To analyze the law of copyright and attain a balance between the copyright owner and the user
To analyze the law of trademarks and attain a balance between the trademark owner and the general public
To analyze the law of insolvency and attain a balance of interests among different stakeholders

ACCT 2010.title: Principles of Accounting I
ACCT 2010.description: For SB&M students, and programs that designate the course as a required/specified elective course. This is the first course of the principles of accounting sequence. Introduction to the concepts and principles of financial accounting, including the analysis, recording, and reporting of business transactions and preparation of financial statements.
cilos: Understanding Basic Accounting Concepts.
Transaction Analysis: Apply conceptual knowledge to business transactions and translate them into financial statements.
Financial Statements Preparation: Learn to prepare and understand the four major financial statements: Balance Sheet, Income Statement, Statement of Cash Flows, and Statement of Stockholder’s Equity.
Financial Statement Analysis: Demonstrate the skills to read, analyze, and interpret financial statements and key financial ratios.
Understanding Ethical Principles: Recognize the importance of ethics in accounting and the impact of ethical (unethical) behaviors on financial reporting and business practices.

ACCT 2200.title: Principles of Accounting II
ACCT 2200.description: For SB&M students, and programs that designate the course as a required/specified elective course. This is the second course of the principles of accounting sequence. It introduces concepts, accounting methods, and analytical tools related to managerial and cost accounting. Topics include fundamental cost concepts, job-order and process costing systems, CVP analysis, budgets and standards, segment reporting, and decision-making using cost information.
cilos: Define and classify cost accounting concepts used by managers.
Apply and analyze various costing methods to calculate and interpret costs used by manufacturing organizations.
Analyze different types of cost behaviors and evaluate the relationships between cost, volume, and profit.
Apply management accounting principles to analyze and interpret relevant information for effective decision-making.
Understand the benefits of budgeting and prepare the master budget.
Understand how standard costs are determined and variances are investigated.
Understand how management accounting utilizes financial accounting information for the measurement of the performance of individuals and business segments.
Understand and apply various capital budgeting tools.

ACCT 3010.title: Financial Accounting I
ACCT 3010.description: Study of the application of generally accepted accounting principles to accounting for business organizations; evaluation of balance sheet accounts and the related effects on income determination.
cilos: Think critically and creatively and make effective decisions supported by analytical and quantitative techniques.
Demonstrate an ability to understand in-depth grasp of financial accounting frameworks.
Demonstrate sophisticated user of financial accounting information by interpreting financial strategies, assess financial risk and understand financial accounting choices made by managers.
Demonstrate an understanding of the international dimensions of accounting.
Understand the role played by accountants in providing and ensuring the integrity of financial and related information.
Demonstrate an understanding of the accounting environment in Hong Kong.
Demonstrate an understanding of ethical challenges, creative accounting, and earnings management issues, and develop ethical and social responsibility.

ACCT 3020.title: Financial Accounting II
ACCT 3020.description: Continuation of ACCT 3010. Special problems in accounting for owner's equity and long-term liabilities including corporate bonds, leases, deferred taxation and pensions.
cilos: Demonstrate an ability to understand in-depth grasp of financial accounting frameworks.
Demonstrate an effective user of financial accounting information by interpreting financial strategies, assess financial risk and understand financial accounting choices made by managers.
Understand the role played by accountants in providing and ensuring the integrity of financial and related information.
Demonstrate an understanding of the international dimensions of accounting.
Demonstrate an understanding of the accounting environment in Hong Kong.

ACCT 3030.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting for Non-Accounting Majors
ACCT 3030.description: Financial accounting concepts and practices with particular emphasis on the analysis and interpretation of financial reports and data.
cilos: Think critically and creatively in making effective decisions supported by analytical and quantitative techniques.
Explain the interdependence and distinctive elements of accounting, finance and economics, and integrate them to solve business problems.
Apply financial accounting frameworks to business situations.

Demonstrate an understanding of the international dimensions of accounting. Identify the activities/issues in accounting that may present ethical challenges, and articulate the consequences associated with unethical behavior.

ACCT 3210.title: Advanced Management Accounting
ACCT 3210.description: This course covers advanced quantitative methods for management decision-making (decision trees, linear regression, learning curves, and linear programming), pricing and transfer pricing decisions, allocation of common and joint costs, variance analysis, performance measurement and incentive compensation.
cilos: Analyze and evaluate a variety of business problems to develop effective and innovative solutions.
Develop leadership skills by solving operational and strategic planning problems.
Demonstrate communication skills through class participation and case discussions.

ACCT 3610.title: Business Law
ACCT 3610.description: This course is to provide students with an awareness of the overall legal framework in which businesses in Hong Kong operate so as to enable them to apply the relevant laws and practices to business problems and practical solutions. The main objective is to give students an understanding of how the society and business function in different socio-legal contexts like the legal system and process and its influence on citizens’ social rights and duties; the enforcement and honoring of agreement between private citizens, the use of business organizations in commercial society, the relationship between employee and employer from social and legal perspectives, the growing importance of business ethics and corporate social responsibilities etc.
cilos: Analyze the principal concepts of the contract law.
Analyze the principal concepts of the law of tort and negligence.
Analyze the principal concepts of the consumer laws.
Analyze the principal aspects of regulations that govern the different business organizations.
Analyze the principal concepts of the employment laws.
Understand the principal concepts of the data protection laws.

ACCT 3630.title: ESG Measurement, Disclosure and Applications
ACCT 3630.description: Environment, Society and Governance (ESG) are three pillars in the emerging system of sustainable finance. This course is designed for students interested in the concept of ESG, especially for those who aspire to learn about the measurement and disclosure of ESG and their applications in the management of business and investment. The course covers topics such as the history and regulations of sustainable finance, the concept and measurement of ESG risks, the disclosure framework and ratings of ESG, the ESG-related investing approaches and financial products. It also covers how management can integrate climate-related risks into business strategies and capture low-carbon opportunities. For all UG students in Year 3 or above.
cilos: Understand the concepts of ESG and sustainable finance.
Understand the measurement of ESG factors and analyze their disclosures.
Understand the processes and limitations of ESG ratings.
Understand the concept of climate risks and analyze their disclosures.
Understand how to consider ESG in investing.
Understand how to integrate climate-related risks into business strategy and capture low-carbon opportunities.

ACCT 3880.title: Professional Excellence Program
ACCT 3880.description: Introductory-level seminars and workshops on the accounting/auditing professions; development of life-skills including writing and other communication skills; and individual thinking skills; ethics for accountants. For SB&M students only. Graded P or F.
cilos: Identify and analyze key issues in the contemporary business environment, including those affecting the accounting and finance profession.
Explain how professional accountants would add values in business transactions.
Explain the role played by professional accountants in providing and ensuring the integrity of financial and related information.
Appreciate the multi-disciplinary approach to solve business problems.
Demonstrate how safeguards could be used to deal with ethical threats.
Demonstrate a sound understanding of contemporary business issues by conducting research on selected topics and presenting original ideas in a logical and creative manner.

ACCT 4010.title: Advanced Financial Accounting
ACCT 4010.description: Addresses accounting issues associated with (1) intercorporate investment activity that conveys significant influence or control and (2) cross-border activities.  The core topics addressed are business combinations, consolidated financial statements, associated companies, and foreign currency issues.
cilos: Develop a comprehensive and well-founded knowledge of advanced financial accounting.
Apply critical and creative thinking to make effective decisions, supported by appropriate analytical and quantitative techniques.
Apply financial accounting frameworks to analyze corporate performance and business situations.
Demonstrate an understanding of the international dimensions of accounting.
Understand ethical and social responsibilities in local and global context.

ACCT 4410.title: Taxation
ACCT 4410.description: The Hong Kong taxation system and its administration; taxation of individuals, partnerships and corporations; stamp duty; obligations compliance.
cilos: Describe the law and practice of Hong Kong tax, including source of tax law; Inland Revenue practices including those dealing with basic principles and practices relating to cross-border transactions between Hong Kong and the Mainland China.

Describe and explain the law, principles and practices of Hong Kong property tax, salaries tax and profit tax, depreciation allowance, personal assessment, tax management, stamp duty and tax administration.
Apply the tax principles to practical business situations and identify issues in income taxes and stamp duty planning.
Explain the law and practice of offence and penalty.
Describe the basic principles and ethical requirements of tax practice.
Demonstarte an ability to communicate effectively in verbal, written and electronic formats.

ACCT 4510.title: Auditing
ACCT 4510.description: Objectives, standards and procedures of auditing; preparation of working papers; applications of statistical sampling; computer-assisted auditing and auditing of electronic data processing (EDP) services; professional liability and ethics.
cilos: Understand the regulatory and professional framework of the auditing profession.

Apply auditing theories, standards, and procedures to the practice of auditing, including designing and implementing methodologies for examining, verifying, evaluating and reporting on the financial statements of organizations.

Identify an ethical dilemma in a scenario case of auditing, articulate the consequences associated with unethical behavior, and apply professional ethical standards to propose and defend a resolution.
Demonstrate critical judgment by analyzing core issues and key assumptions in auditing scenarios, and evaluate problems from multiple perspectives.

ACCT 4610.title: Company Law
ACCT 4610.description: Law relating to companies registered in Hong Kong; company formation and records; share and loan capital; management and administration; reconstructions; mergers and take-overs; liquidation and receivership.
cilos: Explain and apply the process of forming an incorporated body.
Analyse how companies make decisions and manage their activities, and apply the rules and requirements to practical business situations.

Analyse the essential elements of agency relationship, including the role of an agent, how an agency is created, the different types of authority of an agent, and the rights, duties and liabilities of an agent and a principal.
Analyse the legal implications of issuing share capital and loan capital.
Explain and apply the important rules and requirements applicable to public companies in relation to fund-raising, prospectus contents and liabilities, and continuing obligations of listed companies.
Explain and apply the schemes of arrangement, reconstruction, and the take-over provisions of the Companies Ordinance.
Analyse and apply the rules and requirements regarding company liquidation and winding up.

Describe the key roles of external regulatory bodies, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Securities and Futures Commission, the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the Financial Reporting Council and the Insurance Authority.

ACCT 4710.title: Accounting Analytics for Professional Accountants
ACCT 4710.description: Data analytics is reshaping the work of accountants. Applications of data analytics in accounting including: Auditing/Assurance - data analytics techniques used by accounting professionals and auditors nowadays to detect fraud and conduct forensic accounting. Enhancing Financial Reporting: more sophisticated data analytics tools can allow companies to link diverse financial and non-financial datasets and provide more comprehensive and rigorous financial reports to stakeholders. Managing risks: data analytics techniques such as continuous auditing and continuous monitoring can help accounting professionals assess and manage relevant risk levels within their organization. This course aims to provide students with knowledge of the nature and role of data analytics and enable students to apply and understand data analytics technologies to perform audit, enhance financial reporting, and minimize risks as accounting professionals.
cilos: Identify and incorporate useful sources of financial and non-financial data that help accountants' decision-making.
Apply and demonstrate knowledge of the nature and role of accounting data analytics and understand how important it is to accounting professionals.
Use and evaluate analytics techniques to interpret accounting data, analyze business process, and develop solutions for issues in accounting processes.
Utilize data analytics application(s) to perform and develop skills in accounting audit, fraud detection and business analysis.
Diagnose accounting problems and issues by using accounting data analytics to make responsible and ethical decisions.

ACCT 4720.title: Equity Investment with Machine Learning
ACCT 4720.description: This course is designed for students interesting in the investment management business, especially for those who aspire to learn the application of quantitative and machine learning technology in equity investing. The course will cover a wide range of topics in equity investing, including quantitative investment process, multi-factor stock-selection models, portfolio construction methods, performance evaluation, and an introduction of applications of AI/machine learning technology in equity investing. This is a very hands-on course. Students will be required to conduct quantitative and machine learning analyses using Python. Prior knowledge in capital markets and python programing is required. For students in their third year of study and above.
cilos: Understand the philosophy, theory, and process of quantitative equity investing.
Understand the role of financial statement information in equity investing.
Understand the potential application of machine learning technology in equity investment.
Develop investment strategies using accounting and other financial information.
Conduct backtests on quantitative strategies and evaluate their performance.
Articulate the logic of investment strategies and backtest results clearly.

ACCT 4801.title: Cryptocurrency, blockchain and their business applications
ACCT 4801.description: This course introduces cryptocurrencies (including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and others), blockchain, also known as distributed ledger technology (DLT), and their multidimensional business applications. Student will be equipped with fundamental skills to comprehend cryptocurrencies and blockchain/DLT, and be provided with insights into the latest development in the field. For ACCT students in their third year of study or above only. Other students in their third year of study or above may seek instructor’s approval for enrollment in the course.
cilos: Understand the technical details and consensus mechanisms of cryptocurrencies.
Familiar with real-world applications of blockchain technology.
Understand smart contract and its implications for accounting, finance and economics.
Know the history of blockchain technology and its recent development including regulations.

ACCT 4802.title: Valuation and Risk Management in Mergers and Acquisitions
ACCT 4802.description: This course is designed to enhance student ability in reading, understanding and analyzing complicated financial statements that involve mergers and acquisitions (M&A) based on a number of case studies, and to benefit any student who desires to increase his or her ability to profitably exploit financial information that involves complex financial scenarios, such as M&A. In addition, students are expected to integrate accounting with insights from financial economics to understand and analyze economic incentives and risk factors of M&A, therefore converting accounting data into decision making information and express strategic business plans and investment ideas in a powerful and convincing way. For ACCT students in their third year of study or above only.
cilos: Understand latest financial reporting rules for M&A deals.
Understand how synergies impact value creation.
Understand operational, financial and governance risks involved in M&A deals and responding risk management strategies.
Effectively analyze complicated financial statements to assess synergy, value growth, and risks of M&A.

ACCT 4803.title: Artificial Intelligence for Accounting Practice and Analysis
ACCT 4803.description: This course will put the current uses of artificial intelligence (AI) in the context of its development at the nexus of cognitive science, computer science, cybernetics (the study of complex systems), and statistics. Within this framework, the course will explore modern applications of AI, large language models (LLMs), and agentic systems to Accounting Practice and analysis. Particular emphasis will be placed on their usage in current business applications and their potential to shape the future of work for Accounting graduates. The course will also introduce basic skills for implementing and automating LLM-based analysis tasks. For ACCT students in their third year of study or above only.
cilos: Understand AI as an interdisciplinary field, its history and future.
Understand the technical details of current AI tools.
Gain experience implementing and evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of current tools.
Explore current applications of AI to real business problems.

ACCT 4804.title: Forensic Accounting and Fraud Detection
ACCT 4804.description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of forensic accounting and its role in addressing financial crime. It provides an overview of fraud and other financial misconduct, the responsibilities of forensic professionals, and the legal and regulatory frameworks that guide their work. Students will explore fraud risk management, investigative processes, evidence analysis, and effective reporting techniques, along with emerging issues such as cybercrime and digital fraud. The course also examines damages quantification, and the broader strategies organizations use to prevent, detect, and respond to financial crime. It prepares students with the foundational knowledge and practical skills needed to operate in forensic, compliance, and risk management roles. For ACCT students in their third year of study or above only.
cilos: Explain the principles, roles, and regulatory framework of forensic accounting and fraud examination.
Identify and assess financial crime risks.
Plan, conduct, and document forensic investigations.
Analyze financial harm and develop mitigation strategies.

ACCT 4980.title: Independent Study
ACCT 4980.description: Directed study of selected problems in accounting not covered in other courses. Graded letter grade or P/F subject to different offerings.
cilos: Demonstrate an in-depth and substantial knowledge on the topic chosen for the independent study.
Develop and demonstrate critical thinking skills.
Integrate knowledge from a range of fields to effectively communicate key issues from the chosen area of study.

ACCT 5100.title: Corporate Reporting
ACCT 5100.description: Introduction to accounting concepts, preparation and interpretation of financial statements. This is a core course for MBA and MSc(FINA).
cilos: Compare and contrast the balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows.
Explain the economic environment of corporate financial reporting.
Infer economic events from financial statements.
Analyze a company’s financial health and provide a reasoned basis for the conclusions.
Adjust financial statements to make them more useful for decision making needs.
Recognize the most common cases of accounting frauds.
Describe the most common trading rules based on accounting information.

ACCT 5100.title: Corporate Reporting
ACCT 5100.description: Introduction to accounting concepts, preparation and interpretation of financial statements. This is a core course for MBA.
cilos: Compare and contrast the balance sheet, income statement, and statement of cash flows.
Explain the economic environment of corporate financial reporting.
Infer economic events from financial statements.
Analyze a company’s financial health and provide a reasoned basis for the conclusions.
Adjust financial statements to make them more useful for decision making needs.
Recognize the most common cases of accounting frauds.
Describe the most common trading rules based on accounting information.

ACCT 5140.title: Financial Statement Analysis
ACCT 5140.description: Integrated analysis of industry strategy, accounting policy, financial ratios and cash flows for application in equity valuation, credit analysis and bond ratings.  Essential for those planning careers in financial management, investment analysis, credit analysis, business valuation, and consulting.
cilos: Use alternative measures of profitability and financial ratios to evaluate firm performance and identify investment targets.
Use financial ratios and price multiples to determine the timing of investment.
Use financial ratios to forecast financial statements and conduct credit analysis.
Understand how managers can use discretions in accounting method choices and estimates to influence financial statements and how to make adjustment to conduct meaningful comparisons.
Understand the difference between net income and cash flow from operations and how to use it and other indicators to detect accounting manipulation.

ACCT 5150.title: Accounting Foundations
ACCT 5150.description: Introduction to accounting concepts, preparation and interpretation of financial statements.
cilos: Compare and contrast the balance sheets, income statements, statements of shareholders’ equity, and statements of cash flows.
Explain the economic environment of corporate financial reporting.
Infer economic events from financial statements.
Analyze a company’s financial health and provide a reasoned basis for the conclusions.
Adjust financial statements to make them more useful for decision making needs.
Recognize the most common cases of accounting frauds.
Describe the most common trading rules based on accounting information.

ACCT 5160.title: Corporate Financial Reporting I
ACCT 5160.description: Corporate financial reporting from the perspective of managers and financial statement users, including analysts. Topics include inventories, fixed assets, income taxes, liabilities, leases, off-balance-sheet debt, and dilutive securities.
cilos: Think critically and creatively and use analytical and quantitative techniques to make effective decisions.
Explain the financial accounting frameworks.
Use financial accounting information sophisticatedly, interpret financial strategies, assess financial risk and analyze financial accounting choices made by managers.
Recognize the international dimensions of accounting.
Define the role played by accountants in providing and ensuring the integrity of financial and related information.
Describe the accounting environment in Hong Kong.
Identify ethical challenges, creative accounting, and earnings management issues, and develop ethical and social responsibility.

ACCT 5170.title: Corporate Financial Reporting II
ACCT 5170.description: Corporate financial reporting from the perspective of managers and financial statement users, including analysts.  Topics include intercorporate investments, business combinations, multinational operations, pensions, and earnings quality.
cilos: Think critically and creatively and use analytical and quantitative techniques to make effective decisions.
Explain the financial accounting frameworks.
Use financial accounting information sophisticatedly, interpret financial strategies, assess financial risk and analyze financial accounting choices made by managers.
Recognize the international dimensions of accounting.
Define the role played by accountants in providing and ensuring the integrity of financial and related information.
Identify ethical challenges, creative accounting, and earnings management issues, and develop ethical and social responsibility.

ACCT 5180.title: Advanced Corporate Financial Reporting
ACCT 5180.description: Reporting of business entities with inter-corporate investments in subsidiaries and/or associated companies and cross-border activities. Topics include business combinations, consolidated financial statements, equity accounting, and translations of foreign currency transactions.
cilos: Discuss financial reporting practices by referring to the Conceptual Framework.
Explain the international dimensions of accounting.
Assess financial strategies and risk management policies of business entities with inter-corporate investments that convey control and/or significant influence and cross-border activities.
Demonstrate the roles of accountants in providing and ensuring the integrity of financial and related information.
Identify ethical challenges, creative accounting, and earnings management issues, and point out ethical and social responsibility of entities.
Analyze financial reporting issues, and propose and explain solutions thereof, in a team environment.

ACCT 5210.title: Managerial Accounting Foundations
ACCT 5210.description: Use of accounting data in decision-making, financial planning, control, and performance evaluation within organizations.
cilos: Interpret and explain cost concepts and related terms.
Interpret cost-volume-profit analysis.
Estimate the cost and price of a product.
Apply core managerial accounting information to strategic decision making.
Identify the internal budgeting process.
Construct cost management tools such as Activity-Based Costing.
Organize managerial accounting information to conduct performance evaluations.
Identify managerial accounting information as a competitive tool.

ACCT 5220.title: International Treasury Management
ACCT 5220.description: Specialized knowledge in international treasury operation and management control, risk management, inflation and foreign currency changes as well as international transfer pricing.
cilos: Facilitate students to topics related to treasury management and its international issues.
Expose students to working capital management and related international financial management issues.
Facilitate students to financial statement issues related foreign currency translation in consolidated financial statements and inflation restatement in price level changes.
Expose students to international transfer pricing issues related to international duty and tax.
Expose students to management internal control and risk management issues in international field.
Facilitate students to management control related to international management accounting issues.

ACCT 5320.title: Beyond the Headlines: Financial Reporting and Valuation Issues in M&A
ACCT 5320.description: Financial accounting is the fundamental language used to express the economic realities of complex financial scenarios including mergers & acquisitions (M&A) and corporate divestitures. Understanding this language is crucial for converting financial statement data into decision enhancing information, and expressing strategic business plans and investment ideas in a powerful and convincing way. The course is designed to develop sophisticated users of financial accounting information and will benefit any student who desires to increase his or her ability to understand and profitably exploit financial information. The class format involves a mixture of lecture and class discussion.
cilos: Differentiate implications for firms operating under various influence and control situations.
Recognize the latest financial reporting rules for M&A deals.
List tax structuring and tax implications of M&A deals.
Analyze M&A risk management including earn-outs, contingent value rights, and collars.

ACCT 5330.title: Financial Institutions: Fundamental Analysis and Risk Management
ACCT 5330.description: This course covers financial statement analysis and risk management practices for financial institutions, with an emphasis on global banks. It aims to provide students with a solid grounding in the critical evaluation of banks’ financial performance, accounting practices, and risk management.
cilos: Describe the major types and key functions of financial institutions.
Analyze financial statements and accounting practices of banks.
Evaluate regulatory compliance and financial performance of banks.
Assess bank valuation and identify key factors.
Be familiar with bank risk management framework and practices.

ACCT 5410.title: Taxation
ACCT 5410.description: The course introduces the fundamentals of Hong Kong taxation based on case law and legislation. Topics include: property tax, salaries tax, profits tax, depreciation allowances, personal assessment, and stamp duty.
cilos: Recognize the basic principles of Hong Kong taxation and operation of the tax system.
Compute the tax liabilities for individuals and companies.
Explain the tax implications of transactions on business activities.
Apply their tax knowledge to tax cases and in real-life contexts.

ACCT 5430.title: Tax and Business Strategy
ACCT 5430.description: This course provides students with the framework of strategic tax planning. Students learn how to integrate the role of tax in various corporate decision-making.
cilos: Apply the framework of strategic tax planning.
Analyze how taxes impact choices of organizational forms.
Evaluate the role of tax in corporate investment and financing decisions.
Analyze cross-border tax planning opportunities for multinationals.
Explain the ethics of tax planning.

ACCT 5440.title: International Taxation
ACCT 5440.description: This course provides students with an understanding of the basic principles of international taxation and implementation in local jurisdictions. The course focuses on frameworks set forth by international bodies in addressing taxation issues from a global perspective. Topics covered in this course include double taxation, transfer pricing, income tax treaties, sources of income, and tax avoidance issues. Some country-specific tax principles would also be covered. This is a comprehensive taxation course that aims at giving students a high-level understanding of international landscape that enables them to make inquiry based on their foundational knowledge when making business decision as an accounting professional/finance executive.
cilos: Understand international tax regimes and their application in local jurisdictions.
Understand some basic principles of international taxation and comprehend different tax systems.
Apply international tax regimes to business with global operations.
Analyze planning or structuring opportunities to optimize tax efficiency of business with global operations.
Evaluate impact on business under different international tax regimes.

ACCT 5510.title: Auditing
ACCT 5510.description: It covers the relevant principles, objectives and ethical requirements of audit and assurance services; identifies the audit process from client acceptance, design of audit procedures and express an appropriate audit conclusion based on the audit evidence obtained. Topics include: audit planning, audit evidence and documentation, internal control, completion of audit, audit opinion and reporting, professional ethics, rights and obligation of auditors.
cilos: Describe the auditing profession, and the regulatory, legal and reporting framework of auditing.
Recognize the basic principles, objectives and ethical requirements of audit and assurance services.
Identify the audit process from client acceptance, design of audit procedures and recommend an appropriate audit conclusion based on the audit evidence obtained.
Assess risks and threats to an audit of financial statements through analytical and critical thinking.
Communicate effectively in writing and verbally.

ACCT 5630.title: Business Law
ACCT 5630.description: This course is designed for the study of Business Law with practical examples of the application of law in the real business world. The course materials cover  topics highly relevant to the business managers in the decision making process. The end goal is to elevate the student's level of understanding of the surrounding legal environment.
cilos: Apply the legal knowledge studied to situations they are likely to encounter in their daily life and future careers.
Recognize the importance of different functional areas of the law, and solve legal and business problems critically and creatively by referring to the well-established cases and ordinances.
Recognize the importance of the law of professional negligence and duty of care on the part of the accountants and auditors, and become a responsible and capable member of the accounting profession.
Develop selected skills like analytical and critical thinking, effective communication and team work through the group project and presentation.
Recognize the importance of ethical responsibility, identify the ethical dilemmas, apply the ethical standards and recognize the consequences of breaching the ethical standards.
Recognize the importance of ethical responsibility and corporate social responsibility in the context of Chinese business ethics.

ACCT 5640.title: Company Law
ACCT 5640.description: Law relating to companies registered in Hong Kong; company formation and records; share and loan capital; management and administration; reconstructions; mergers and take-overs; liquidation and receivership.
cilos: Explain the documents that lay down the features of a company and its internal procedures, and evaluate whether they can be altered.
Explain the role of key personnel in the management and administration of a company, and judge their rights and obligations.
Apply the rules in relation to company meetings.
Explain legal considerations and apply the legal rules in raising share or loan capital.
Explain the schemes of arrangement and apply the Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy-backs.
Explain the law in relation to commencement, conduct and consequences of winding up and apply the avoidance powers.
Explain the role, structure, duties, powers and procedures of some important external bodies in relation to the work of an accountant.

ACCT 5650.title: Corporate Governance
ACCT 5650.description: The course covers corporate governance at two levels. At the foundation level, it introduces students to the core principles and values of corporate governance, and various requirements of compliance by company boards as stipulated in different regulatory frameworks. At the more advanced level, this course introduces students to broader aspects of corporate governance, focusing on the latest discussions and development of corporate governance resulting from promulgation and interaction of stakeholders worldwide.
cilos: Describe the background of development of corporate governance, and its importance to the sustainability of businesses by way of protecting stakeholders’ interests.

Explain the objectives and roles of directors, accountants and other responsible persons in the corporate governance system, and how stakeholders’ interests can be protected under different corporate governance theories and models.
Comply with the legal and regulatory framework for governance of companies in Hong Kong, while acknowledging recent developments in China and other countries.
Promulgate corporate governance principles and best practice.
Apply probity and ethical standards in governance.
Assert the value and importance of internal control functions and risk management to sound corporate governance.
Explain corporate social responsibility and its emerging importance to modern businesses, and recent developments in related corporate governance practice.

ACCT 5650.title: Corporate Governance and Compliance
ACCT 5650.description: The course covers corporate governance at two levels. At the practice level, it builds on students' prior knowledge of company law, and introduces them to the various requirements of compliance by company boards as stipulated in the Hong Kong regulatory framework. At the company policies level, this course introduces students to broader aspects of corporate governance, focusing on the multitude and interaction of stakeholders and how their interests may be protected.
cilos: Describe the background of development of corporate governance, and its importance to the sustainability of businesses by way of protecting stakeholders’ interests.

Explain the objectives and roles of directors, accountants and other responsible persons in the corporate governance system, and how stakeholders’ interests can be protected under different corporate governance theories and models.
Comply with the legal and regulatory framework for governance of companies in Hong Kong, while acknowledging recent developments in China and other countries.
Promulgate corporate governance principles and best practice.
Apply probity and ethical standards in governance.
Assert the value and importance of internal control functions and risk management to sound corporate governance.
Explain corporate social responsibility and its emerging importance to modern businesses, and recent developments in related corporate governance practice.

ACCT 5710.title: Data Analytics in Accounting
ACCT 5710.description: Data analytics is the process of collecting, organizing and analyzing big data in order to discover useful information for different uses. This course aims to provide students with knowledge of the nature and role of data analytics and how important it is to accountants, and enable students to apply and understand big data issues and utilize data mining, data modeling, data analysis and data visualization techniques to solve accounting and business related issues.
cilos: Explain and define the nature and role of data analytics and its application in accounting and business.
Explain and define issues related to big data and how to utilize big data.
Apply data mining modeling, analysis, and visualization techniques to solve accounting and business issues.
Utilize data analytics application(s) to perform and develop skills in business analysis.
Diagnose problems and issues by using big data to make responsible and ethical decisions.

ACCT 5720.title: Advanced Data Analytics in Accounting
ACCT 5720.description: With the foundation of ACCT 5710 Data Analytics in Accounting, this course aims to provide students with advanced and practical knowledge of applications in data analytics designed by accounting professionals and enable students to apply and understand data analytics technologies to perform audit, enhance financial reporting, and minimize risks as accounting professionals.
cilos: Describe and apply knowledge and accounting applications on common ERP capabilities - collection, cleaning and analysis of data.
Identify common data analytics challenges and risks in accounting issues.
Utilize and apply accounting data analytics and its applications on modeling patterns of data, and identifying outliers and anomalies.
Apply and evaluate accounting analytics techniques on analysis for fraudulent activities in corporations.
Identify and incorporate accounting analytics technology and options for visualizations.
Identify and explain accounting issues in decision making in the data age - the future of data analytics in accounting.

ACCT 5730.title: Equity Investment with Machine Learning
ACCT 5730.description: This course introduces the application of quantitative and machine learning technology in equity investing. It covers classical equity valuation theories, cutting-edge capital market research and recent development in quantitative and machine learning technology. Students will be required to apply the knowledge to develop and test equity investment strategies.
cilos: Describe the current landscape and challenges of the asset management industry.
Explain the philosophy, theory, and process of quantitative equity investing.
Evaluate the performance of equity funds and investment strategies.
Be familiar with multifactor stock-selection models.
Identify the potential applications of machine learning technology in equity investment.
Design and develop quantitative investment strategies.
Conduct backtests on quantitative strategies and evaluate their performance.

ACCT 5801.title: Cryptocurrency, Blockchain and Their Business Applications
ACCT 5801.description: This course discusses cryptocurrencies (including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and others), blockchain, also known as distributed ledger technology (DLT), and their multidimensional business applications. The course provides a basic set of skills to understand cryptocurrencies and blockchain/DLT. We will also discuss the latest development in the field.
cilos: Describe the history of blockchain technology and its recent development.
Explain the technical details of blockchain/distributed ledger technology including consensus mechanisms.
Identify real-world applications of blockchain technology.
Understand smart contracts.
Recognize regulations on cryptocurrency.

ACCT 5901.title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) in China
ACCT 5901.description: This course aims at equipping the next-generation business leaders with knowledge and competence to navigate the nascent, rapidly evolving environmental, social, and governance (ESG) landscape in China, effectively assess and manage the rising ESG risks and opportunities, and seek long-term value creation by taking into account the needs of all their stakeholders and society at large.
cilos: Understand and apply fundamental concepts and analytical tools related to ESG and corporate sustainability.
Analyze and evaluate the strategies and practices of leading companies in sustainable supply chain management, ESG ratings and investing, ESG disclosure, and sustainability reporting.
Understand the science and public policy underlining climate change and apply the corporate strategies for mitigating and adapting to climate change.
Identify and assess the driving forces behind ESG adoption and expansion at the levels of individual firms, specific industries, and an industrializing country as a whole.
Evaluate and rate the ESG practices and reporting of a China-based listed company, while offering innovative and practical solutions for improvement.

ACCT 5902.title: ESG Measurement, Disclosure and Applications
ACCT 5902.description: Environment, Society and Governance (ESG) are three pillars in the emerging field of sustainable finance. This course will cover topics such as the concepts of ESG factors, their importance in business management and investing decisions, how to measure and evaluate ESG risks and opportunities, the global ESG disclosure frameworks, ESG ratings, and how to integrate ESG considerations into investment strategies and design financial products. In addition, the course will cover the concepts, measurement and reporting of climate risk and greenhouse gas emissions.
cilos: Understand the background and history of sustainable development goals and sustainable finance.
Measure and verify the information of greenhouse gas emissions.
Analyze the company’s climate risks and performance from Climate Report.
Analyze the company’s sustainability risks and performance from Sustainability Report.
Use ESG ratings to measure the company’s ESG risks and performance.
Incorporate ESG information in investing decisions.
Evaluate the value and limitations of ESG in management and investing.

ACCT 5920.title: Introduction to Financial Crime
ACCT 5920.description: This introductory course explores into the dynamics of financial crime, its detection, and prevention. Spanning historical perspectives, legal frameworks, and investigation techniques, students will explore the multifaceted nature of financial crime including money laundering, tax evasion, bribery, and corruption. The course integrates criminology and psychological theories to understand offender behavior, alongside the use of professional investigative skills. The course also places emphasis on responsibilities of financial institutions in monitoring and reporting suspicious activities, employing customer due diligence including conducting investigations into beneficial owners and politically exposed persons.
cilos: Understand the historical development and criminalization of financial crime, including what is shadow economy, and the responsibilities of financial institutions in detecting and reporting suspicious activities.
Critically apply criminology theories to understand the motivations and behaviors of offenders in financial crime.
Understand and apply critical thinking, professional skepticism and various financial crime investigation methodologies effectively.
Utilize and analyze financial flow diagrams, associated matrices, and real-world cases to understand money laundering, and spot and investigate complex money laundering schemes.
Apply Customer Due Diligence (CDD), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), sources of funds (SOF), Net Wealth assessments in mitigating and identifying suspicious financial flows.

ACCT 5930.title: Financial Crime Regulation, Compliance and Sanctions
ACCT 5930.description: In today's interconnected world, combating financial crime requires a deep understanding of international regulations, enforcement processes, and emerging trends. This comprehensive course delves into the intricate landscape of financial crime prevention, investigation, and prosecution on a global scale. Students will explore the roles and responsibilities of key agencies, analyze Anti-Money Laundering (AML)/ Counter Terrorism Finance (CTF) frameworks across different jurisdictions, and dissect the anatomy of money laundering prosecutions. From compliance standards to the confiscation of proceeds of crime, this course offers a thorough examination of the tools and strategies employed to tackle financial crime effectively.
cilos: Explain the fundamental principles underlying transnational crime, such as organized crime, terrorism, and war and conflict.
Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of international financial crime regulations.
Acquire a comprehensive toolkit of techniques and strategies for preventing, detecting, and investigating financial crime.
Critically analyze the responses demonstrated by law enforcement agencies and other relevant entities in addressing the challenges posed by financial crime.

ACCT 5940.title: Financial Crime Transaction Monitoring and Investigation
ACCT 5940.description: Money laundering is a common financial crime methodology to integrate the illicit funds from a variety of predicate offences. in this comprehensive course, theoretical knowledge is integrated with practical application and relevant case studies to teach a variety of common types of money laundering schemes. Students will also learn strategies for detecting, investigating and reporting financial crimes.
cilos: Differentiate and explain the features and red flags associated with simple and complex money laundering operations.

Describe and differentiate the roles of various personnel, including board of directors, management, internal auditors, front line staff, and cybersecurity professionals, in the fight against financial crime.
Relate and explain what transaction monitoring is, its purpose and importance as part of financial crime risk management.

Compose an effective Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) Report which complies with legislative requirements and assess what constitutes "reasonable grounds for suspicion" that money or property being processed relates to the proceeds of crime.
Differentiate between a SAR Report and other reporting requirements and describe the risks of not reporting or submitting incomplete reports.

ACCT 5950.title: Financial Crime Risk Management and Governance
ACCT 5950.description: Rapid advances in technology in recent years have helped increase corporate productivity and enabled a global reach for companies, but such advances have also exposed them to criminal and fraudulent behavior. This course takes an advanced approach to managing and identifying risks associated with financial crime activities via the use of entity wide risk management and governance framework. The role of internal controls, governance, monitoring and communication responsibilities are also covered in the course.
cilos: Discuss the origins and key concepts of risk, risk management and risk management standards.
Explain the significance of issues of culture, appetite, and tolerance in managing risks, including their impact on a firm's financial reporting.

Evaluate the key features of corporate governance models, and the relationships between governance, risk oversight, board, management, internal control and assurance, and how they fit in the management and  reporting of financial crime risks.
Recognize and describe common mechanisms for illicitly moving money and schemes leading to occupational and financial statement fraud.

ACCT 5960.title: Data Analytics for Financial Crime Investigation
ACCT 5960.description: This course undertakes a systematic approach to the study of the theory and practice of financial crime investigation. The overall outcome of the course is to equip students with the tools and skills to detect and report financial crime. It aims to provide an understanding of common types of financial crime perpetrated, and to introduce students to strategies and techniques for detecting, investigating, and reporting financial crime as well as for preventing and deterring it.
cilos: Define key concepts and typologies of modern slavery and human trafficking and recognize relevant red flags.
Describe the impact of environmental crimes and explain the nexus between environmental crimes and financial crimes.
Identify and discuss some applications of data visualization, social network analysis, AI and machine learning in an AML/CTF approach.
Utilize analytical software to assist in forensic financial crime investigation.

ACCT 6900.title: Special Topics
ACCT 6900.description: Selected topics in an identified area of accounting. This course may be repeated for credit if based on a different selection of topics.
cilos: Demonstrate a sound grasp of the literature in their specialization.
Apply their specialized knowledge to solve related business problems in an innovative fashion.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of core business functions.
Integrate functional knowledge to solve business problems within their area of specialization.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

ACCT 7710.title: Doctoral Seminar - Selected Topics in Accounting Research
ACCT 7710.description: Discussion of selected research topics in accounting research. Examples of topics covered include classical accounting theories and the application of emerging technological advancements in accounting research. The course focuses on how to apply theory or tools to examine important issues in accounting research.
cilos: Demonstrate a sound grasp of the literature in their specialized area of accounting research.
Apply their specialized knowledge to solve related business problems in an innovative fashion.
Demonstrate a broad based knowledge of core business functions related to accounting research.
Integrate functional knowledge to solve business problems within their specialized area of accounting research.
Present their discipline knowledge clearly to layman.

ACCT 7720.description: Discussion of research in managerial accounting, auditing and corporate governance. Use of analytical and empirical tools in economics, finance and statistics to examine important accounting issues in the above areas.

ACCT 7730.description: Use of empirical and analytical research methods in economics, finance, and statistics to examine important financial accounting issues.
